routing_warnings.description: The client authoritatively accepts two exact passage rewrites; preserving those approved wordings in the final file belongs to manuscript content integrity.
The missing content updates and instruction to use the newly supplied working document concern authoritative final-file content rather than general copyediting quality.
Designating the authoritative working file belongs to final manuscript content integrity.

The broad completion claim refers to the three file-specific corrections enumerated in message 154 and is better handled with the authorized-content lifecycle rather than duplicated as another general copyediting claim.
Confirmation of the final authoritative file concerns manuscript content integrity rather than editorial polish.
The client's statement that the editing looks good evaluates editorial quality rather than confirming retention of the complete authorized revision set.
The request to scan the manuscript for duplicate full stops is a proofreading obligation rather than a change to the authoritative-content mechanism.
The terse removal claim immediately follows the duplicate-full-stop scan request and is better evaluated under manuscript proofreading.
The client's decision to preserve the current title-and-author arrangement concerns page layout rather than the integrity of the title text.
This message assigns a specific image to the GiftingRight chapter, which is chapter-image mapping rather than general suitability review.
This message establishes that an image appears at the beginning of every chapter.
The elongated and cropped-image observations concern rendering defects rather than image suitability.
The client's full-page presentation choice changes chapter-image placement.
The freelancer specifically claims that the images will be formatted for full-page placement.
The requested pixelation check is an image-rendering quality criterion.
The curved corner artifacts and partially cut images are concrete rendering failures.
The separate clause requiring one image for the book cover concerns the paperback-cover Requirement.
The elongated and cropped chapter-image observations concern rendering quality rather than placement.
This implementation explanation concerns placement of the proposed cover image on the first page.
The requested pixelation check concerns image-rendering quality rather than full-page placement itself.
The corner artifacts and partially cut images are rendering defects, not changes to the placement Requirement.
The dedication update in this message concerns final manuscript content rather than special-section typography.
The duplicate-full-stop correction concerns copyediting rather than special-section typography.

The Chapter 14 title and broader chapter-title, subtitle, and table-of-contents review clauses concern heading and TOC typography; only the request to add manuscript page numbers applies to the target Requirement.
The client asks for advice about required front and back matter rather than requesting preparation of the back-matter deliverable.
The publication-readiness statement is based on completed flow and repetition edits and is better treated as a copyediting implementation claim than as delivery of general publishing guidance.
The request for a recommended book size concerns the narrower paperback format and trim-size Requirement.
The question about the author's name at the top of the first page belongs to the title-and-author page layout Requirement.
The request to add page numbers belongs to the pagination Requirement.
The request to review the table of contents belongs to the table-of-contents typography Requirement.
This message concerns updating Table-of-Contents page numbers rather than Table-of-Contents typography.
This response describes when page numbers can be added and does not establish a Table-of-Contents typography requirement.
The statement that the other pages are justified concerns body-text alignment and should not be encoded as an attribute of copyright-page alignment.
